mainTopic: Guarantees (אחריות) and creditors: whose debts a seller's guarantee covers, orphans' movable property, and collecting from later buyers of the borrower's land.
overview: The amud opens at the end of רמי בר חמא's case. ראובן sold a field to שמעון with no guarantee, and שמעון sold it back with a guarantee. רמי בר חמא rules that when ראובן's own creditor seizes it, שמעון must pay ראובן back. רבא objects that a seller's guarantee covers outside creditors, not the buyer's own debts. He agrees, though, that if the creditor belonged to יעקב, the father ראובן inherited from, שמעון must pay, because יעקב's creditor counts as an outsider. Next comes a new case from רמי בר חמא. ראובן's orphans can collect the unpaid price from שמעון even though ראובן's creditor took the field, because orphans' movable property is not tied to a creditor. רבא advises שמעון to pay them in land and then take it back, based on רב נחמן's rule. Finally, רבה rules that ראובן's creditor may collect from either buyer, שמעון or לוי, and the גמרא begins limiting this rule by the quality of the land. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא rules that שמעון must compensate ראובן
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of רמי בר חמא's ruling. When ראובן's creditor takes the field from ראובן, שמעון must pay ראובן back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ראובן's creditor came and took the field away from him. The law is that שמעון has to go and pay ראובן back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רמי בר חמא's case. ראובן's own creditor seized the field, and רמי בר חמא says שמעון must compensate ראובן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא reads the guarantee very literally. שמעון sold the field with אחריות, so any seizure means he must pay. ראובן owes שמעון nothing, because his own sale to שמעון had no guarantee.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, someone who is owed money
Seizes or repossesses property to collect a debt
Compensates, pays someone back for a loss

phrases.english: and Reuven's creditor came
and repossessed it from him
the law is that Shimon goes
and compensates him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינָא הוּא דְּאָזֵיל שִׁמְעוֹן וּמְפַצֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רמי בר חמא's ruling, which began just before this part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ראובן's own creditor seizes the field, שמעון must compensate ראובן because of the guarantee he gave.

steps.title: רבא: the guarantee does not cover the buyer's own debts
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that שמעון only took on a general guarantee against outside claims. He never guaranteed against ראובן's own creditors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Fine, שמעון accepted a general guarantee. But did he accept a guarantee against ראובן's own debts?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רמי בר חמא's ruling. He asks whether שמעון's guarantee could really cover a seizure caused by ראובן's own debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the guarantee into two kinds. One is a general guarantee against other people's claims, and the other is a guarantee against the buyer's own debts. A normal seller only takes on the first kind, so שמעון should not have to pay when ראובן's own creditor takes the field.

keyTerms.meaning: A general guarantee against outside creditors
A guarantee against the buyer's own creditors

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is saying שמעון gave no guarantee at all. רבא agrees the guarantee is real. He only says it doesn't stretch to cover ראובן's own debts.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
granted that he accepted a general guarantee,
did he accept a guarantee against Reuven's own creditors?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: נְהִי דְּאַחְרָיוּת דְּעָלְמָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רמי בר חמא's ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling that שמעון must compensate ראובן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A seller's guarantee covers claims from outsiders. It does not cover a seizure caused by the buyer's own debt.

steps.title: רבא agrees when the creditor belonged to יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees with רמי בר חמא in one case. If ראובן inherited the field from יעקב and יעקב's creditor seizes it, שמעון must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא agrees in this case: ראובן inherited a field from יעקב and sold it to שמעון without a guarantee. Then שמעון sold it back to ראובן with a guarantee. Then יעקב's creditor came and took it from ראובן. Here the law is that שמעון must go and pay ראובן back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us where רבא would agree with רמי בר חמא. The case is one where the creditor belonged to יעקב, the earlier owner, and not to ראובן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from the first case is whose creditor seized the field. Here the debt came from יעקב. Even though ראובן inherited from יעקב, רבא agrees that שמעון's guarantee covers this seizure.

phrases.english: And Rava agrees regarding Reuven
who inherited a field from Ya'akov,
and sold it to Shimon without a guarantee,
and Shimon came and sold it to Reuven with a guarantee,
and Ya'akov's creditor came,
and repossessed it from him
the law is that Shimon goes
and compensates him for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רָבָא בִּרְאוּבֵן שֶׁיָּרַשׁ שָׂדֶה מִיַּעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבא's objection by showing a case where he agrees that שמעון must pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If יעקב's creditor seizes the field that ראובן inherited, שמעון must compensate ראובן, even according to רבא.

steps.title: Why does רבא agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא agrees in the inheritance case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבא's agreement. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question comes up because ראובן inherited from יעקב, so יעקב's debt could seem like ראובן's own debt. If so, רבא's objection should apply here too.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא makes שמעון pay when יעקב's creditor seizes the field, but not when ראובן's creditor does.

steps.title: יעקב's creditor counts as an outside creditor
steps.stepSummary: יעקב's creditor is treated like any general creditor, so the general guarantee covers him.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב's creditor is like a creditor of the world at large.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יעקב's creditor counts as an outsider. That means שמעון's general guarantee covers him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debt belonged to יעקב, not to ראובן personally. So it falls under the general guarantee (אחריות דעלמא), which רבא agreed שמעון accepted. It is not the buyer's own debt.

keyTerms.meaning: He is like an ordinary outside creditor

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a seller's guarantee covers seizures by outside creditors, including the creditor of a previous owner like יעקב. It does not cover seizures caused by the buyer's own debts.

phrases.english: Ya'akov's creditor
is like a general creditor.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל חוֹב דְּיַעֲקֹב כְּבַעַל חוֹב דְּעָלְמָא דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יעקב's creditor is treated like an outside creditor, so שמעון's general guarantee covers his seizure.

steps.title: The orphans can demand the loan money from שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rules that after ראובן dies, his sons can collect the loan from שמעון. שמעון cannot use the guarantee against them, because the loan money is movable property of orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראובן sold a field to שמעון with a guarantee. שמעון didn't pay, so the price was turned into a loan he owed ראובן. ראובן died. ראובן's creditor came to take the field from שמעון, and שמעון paid him off with money. The law is that ראובן's sons can tell שמעון: 'Our father left movable property with you, the money you owe him. Orphans' movable property is not tied to a creditor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a brand-new case from רמי בר חמא and gives his ruling: the orphans win and can still collect the loan from שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the guarantee (אחריות) means ראובן must pay שמעון back for his loss. But ראובן is dead, and all that is left is the loan money שמעון owes, which counts as מטלטלין. Since a creditor cannot collect from orphans' מטלטלין, שמעון cannot subtract his loss from what he owes.

keyTerms.meaning: With a guarantee: if the field is taken away, the seller pays the buyer back
Turned the unpaid price into a loan the buyer owes
Comes to seize (the field) to collect a debt
Is not tied up for paying a creditor

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'creditor' blocked by the orphans' claim is שמעון himself, because the guarantee makes him a kind of creditor of ראובן's estate.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
Reuven who sold a field to Shimon with a guarantee,
and set up (the price) on him as a loan,
phrases.notes: שמעון didn't pay up front, so the price became a debt he owes ראובן.

phrases.english: and Reuven died,
and a creditor of Reuven came
and was seizing it from Shimon
and (Shimon) paid him off with money —

phrases.aramaic: דִּינָא הוּא דְּאָמְרִי לֵיהּ בְּנֵי רְאוּבֵן:
phrases.english: the law is that Reuven's sons can say to him:
Our father left movable property with you,
phrases.notes: He means the loan money שמעון still owes for the field.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִטַּלְטְלִי דְיַתְמֵי לְבַעַל חוֹב לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִי.
phrases.english: and the movable property of orphans is not tied to a creditor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case from רמי בר חמא, separate from the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן's orphans can collect the loan from שמעון and refuse to repay his loss, because orphans' movable property is not subject to a creditor.

steps.title: רבא's advice: pay the orphans in land, then take it back
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a clever שמעון would pay the orphans with land instead of money, and then collect that land back from them for his loss, following רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the other one (שמעון) is clever, he pays them with land, and then collects it back from them. This follows רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds practical advice that gets שמעון around רמי בר חמא's ruling. He then points to רב נחמן as his source, which the next step quotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orphans' defense only works because the loan money is movable property. If שמעון pays them with land, they now own קרקע. Land of orphans is tied to their father's debts, so שמעון can collect it back for the guarantee.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If the other one is clever,
he pays them with land,
phrases.notes: Instead of paying the loan in cash, שמעון hands the orphans a piece of land.

phrases.english: and then collects it back from them,
in line with Rav Nachman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רמי בר חמא's ruling but shows a way for שמעון to protect himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By paying the orphans in land, שמעון can then collect that land back from them under the guarantee.

steps.title: רב נחמן's rule: a creditor can take land the orphans collected
steps.stepSummary: The source for רבא: when orphans collect land for their father's debt, their father's creditor can collect that land from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Orphans who collected land for a debt owed to their father, the creditor can go back and collect it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב נחמן's rule, which is the basis for רבא's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land the orphans receive to pay their father's loan counts as the father's property. So it is tied to the father's debts, and his creditor can take it. Here שמעון, as holder of the guarantee, is that creditor.

keyTerms.meaning: For a debt owed to their father

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that changing money into land changes whether a creditor can reach it.
steps.whatToRemember: Orphans' movable property is protected from their father's creditors, but land they receive for their father's debt is not.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Orphans who collected land for a debt owed to their father —

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל חוֹב חוֹזֵר וְגוֹבֶה אוֹתָהּ מֵהֶן.
phrases.english: the creditor goes back and collects it from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's advice.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that שמעון can collect back the land he gave the orphans.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: a creditor can collect land that orphans received for their father's debt.

steps.title: ראובן's creditor may collect from either buyer
steps.stepSummary: רבה: ראובן sold all his fields to שמעון, and שמעון sold one to לוי. ראובן's creditor may choose to collect from שמעון or from לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: ראובן sold all his fields to שמעון. Then שמעון sold one field to לוי. ראובן's creditor came. If he wants, he collects from this one. If he wants, he collects from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related case from רבה about a creditor collecting from people who bought the borrower's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of ראובן's fields were tied to his debt before he sold them. So the creditor's claim reaches every one of those fields, whether שמעון still holds it or לוי bought it. He can pick whichever buyer he likes.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wants, he collects from this one

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Reuven who sold all his fields to Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר שִׁמְעוֹן וּמָכַר שָׂדֶה אַחַת לְלֵוִי,
phrases.english: and Shimon then sold one field to Levi,
and Reuven's creditor came —
if he wants, he collects from this one,
if he wants, he collects from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related ruling about a creditor collecting from buyers of the borrower's fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראובן's creditor may collect from שמעון or from לוי, whichever he chooses.

steps.title: The rule applies only when לוי bought medium-quality land
steps.stepSummary: רבה's rule letting the creditor collect from לוי applies only if לוי bought בינונית. If לוי bought עידית or זיבורית, he can say: I bought land that is not yours to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when שמעון sold לוי medium-quality land. But if he sold him the best land or the worst land, לוי can tell the creditor: 'That is exactly why I took the trouble to buy land that is not fit for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on רבה's ruling from Step 9. The creditor can take לוי's field only if that field is medium-quality land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor normally collects from בינונית. So a field of עידית or זיבורית is not the kind of land the creditor would take. לוי can argue that he bought it on purpose so it would be safe from the creditor, and the creditor must go to שמעון instead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We only said this when…' The standard way of limiting an earlier ruling.
Medium-quality land, the kind a creditor normally collects from.
'I took the trouble.' לוי chose this land on purpose.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as cancelling רבה's rule. The rule still stands; the גמרא is only saying when it applies.

phrases.english: And we said this only
phrases.notes: 'This' is רבה's rule that the creditor may collect from לוי.

phrases.english: when he sold him medium-quality land,
but if he sold him best-quality or worst-quality land,
he can say to him:
phrases.notes: לוי is speaking to ראובן's creditor.

phrases.english: For this reason I took the trouble and bought
land that is not fit for you.
phrases.notes: A creditor collects from medium land, so the best or worst field isn't the kind he takes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבה's ruling from Step 9 based on the quality of the land לוי bought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The creditor may collect from לוי only if לוי bought בינונית. If לוי bought עידית or זיבורית, he can send the creditor to שמעון.

steps.title: Even with medium land, only if שמעון was not left with similar medium land
steps.stepSummary: Even when לוי bought בינונית, the creditor may take it only if לוי did not leave שמעון with similar בינונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even with medium-quality land, we said this only when לוי did not leave שמעון with other medium-quality land like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit to רבה's rule. The sentence is setting up the next case, what happens if שמעון was left with similar land, and that case continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the creditor may collect from לוי's field if it is בינונית. Now there is a further condition: this holds only if שמעון has no similar בינונית left. The implication is that if שמעון still has matching land, לוי can send the creditor there.

keyTerms.meaning: Left over. Here it means לוי left this land in שמעון's hands.
Like it, of the same kind and quality.

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule letting the creditor collect from לוי has two limits. לוי's field must be בינונית, and שמעון must not still hold similar בינונית.

phrases.english: And even with medium-quality land, we said this only
when he did not leave
medium-quality land like it,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, which tells us what happens if he did leave such land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, narrower limit on top of Step 10's limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when לוי bought בינונית, the creditor may collect from him only if שמעון was not left with similar בינונית.
